sections.label: CPF transition to LIFE
sections.summary: In 2009, Singapore began moving from the Minimum Sum Scheme, now the Retirement Sum Scheme, to the CPF LIFE annuity scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2009, we started to transition from the Minimum Sum Scheme, now known as the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS), to the CPF LIFE annuity scheme.

sections.label: SEPs MediSave contribution shortfall
sections.summary: About 60% of SEPs, roughly 130,000, do not pay their MediSave contributions in full as a lump sum each year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In any given year, about 60% of SEPs do not make their MediSave contributions in full in a lump sum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is very significant, or about 130,000 of them.

sections.label: Contribute-as-you-Earn pilot amendments
sections.summary: The first set of amendments will allow a pilot Contribute-as-you-Earn (CAYE) scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The first set of amendments will allow for a pilot "Contribute-as-you-Earn" (CAYE) scheme.

sections.label: Pilot start date
sections.summary: The Government plans to start this pilot from 1 January 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government plans to start this pilot from 1 January 2020.

sections.label: CAYE soccer clinic contribution
sections.summary: Under CAYE, the school helps Sam contribute $10 for a two-hour soccer clinic, with MediSave at 10% of income earned, not the total service fee.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With CAYE, the school will help Sam make a contribution of $10 for the two-hour soccer clinic.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Based on his income in the previous year, the MediSave contribution payable is 10% of the income he earns and not the total service fee, which can include expenses.

sections.label: Reduced remaining MediSave contribution
sections.summary: By the CPF statement, schools would have helped him contribute $1,300, 10% of $13,000, reducing the remaining contribution from $3,000 to $1,700.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: By the time the CPF statement arrives, the schools would have helped him contribute $1,300, or 10% of $13,000, throughout the year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And so, as a result, the remaining contribution is no longer $3,000 but a reduced amount of $1,700.

sections.label: SEP MediSave opt-out pilot
sections.summary: SEPs who paid MediSave in full or via instalments may opt out of the pilot.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SEPs who have made their MediSave contributions in full or are keeping up via an instalment plan will be allowed to opt out of this pilot.

sections.label: Support for CAYE pilot SEPs
sections.summary: The Government will look into providing some support for SEPs in the CAYE pilot.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government will look into providing some support for SEPs participating in the CAYE pilot.

sections.label: CPF refund application rules
sections.summary: Amended CPF Act regulations let employees apply for a CPF refund within one year, and employers with consent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Regulations prescribed under the amended CPF Act will give employees flexibility to apply for a refund for the CPF portion within one year of having to return the conditional wage.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Employers may also apply for the refund, with the employee's consent.

sections.label: Daniel's CPF refund application
sections.summary: Daniel may apply to CPF Board to refund $1,850 from his CPF account to his employer.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With this amendment, Daniel may apply to CPF Board to refund the $1,850 from his CPF account to his employer if he wishes.

sections.label: CPF interest practice and RSS review
sections.summary: The amendment regularises CPF Board paying interest until claims are paid, and RSS payout rules are being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In practice, CPF Board has always paid the interest accrued on the outstanding loan all the way until the claim is paid.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In other words, families have not needed to make further payments because of the time it took to report and process the claim.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This amendment simply regularises this practice in the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This sums up the key amendments to the CPF Act.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I will take this opportunity to briefly talk about changes we are making to the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS) in response to feedback from Members.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I shared in a written Parliamentary reply in October that MOM and CPF Board were reviewing the RSS payout rules.

sections.label: Automatic CPF LIFE inclusion
sections.summary: Members with at least $60,000 in their Retirement Account at age 65 are automatically included in CPF LIFE.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Members will be automatically included in CPF LIFE if they have at least $60,000 in their Retirement Account at age 65.

sections.label: RSS payouts last to 90
sections.summary: RSS payouts will be designed to last to age 90 at most, instead of age 95.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The key change we will make is to design RSS payouts such that they will last to age 90 at most, instead of age 95.

sections.label: RSS payout increase example
sections.summary: Under the new RSS payout rules, his payouts will increase from $470 to $520.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under the new RSS payout rules, his payouts will increase from $470 to $520.

sections.label: RSS payout changes in 2020
sections.summary: The changes to how RSS payouts are computed will take effect in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The changes to how RSS payouts are computed will take effect in 2020.

sections.label: 60,000 members payouts increase
sections.summary: Around 60,000 members will see their payouts increase as a result.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Around 60,000 members will see their payouts increase as a result.

sections.label: CAYE scheme MediSave contributions
sections.summary: The CAYE scheme helps SEPs contribute to MediSave when paid for work, with regular contributions from 2020 when the Government pays for their services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The CAYE scheme is designed to help SEPs contribute to their MediSave account as and when they are paid for their work, instead of requiring a yearly lump sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Starting from 2020 onwards, under the CAYE scheme, SEPs will have small and regular contributions made to their MediSave accounts when the Government pays for their services.

sections.label: SEP numbers in Singapore
sections.summary: About 6,000 SEPs provide services directly to the Government and may benefit from CAYE, out of about 200,000 SEPs last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Second, I note that, at present, there are approximately 6,000 SEPs who provide services directly to the Government and, therefore, stand to benefit from the CAYE scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: As of last year, I understand that there were approximately 200,000 SEPs in Singapore's resident workforce.

sections.label: SEPs not employees, CPF
sections.summary: SEPs are not employees and so not entitled to CPF, though some countries treat certain SEPs as employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The root cause of this issue is fundamentally because SEPS, or freelancers, are not employees and, therefore, not entitled to CPF contributions to begin with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, it is worth highlighting that in some countries, such as Norway and Australia, certain classes of SEPs, such as food delivery riders, are now considered "employees" and accorded employee rights and benefits, including the right to join unions.

sections.label: 60% do not contribute
sections.summary: The Minister earlier pointed out that 60% of them do not do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As the Minister rightly pointed out earlier, 60% of them do not do so.

sections.label: Government MediSave contributions for freelancers
sections.summary: The Government wants to help freelancers contribute to MediSave for medical needs through the CAYE scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, as a responsible service buyer, the Government wants to help freelancers make contributions to their MediSave accounts so that they can have adequate savings for medical needs through the CAYE scheme.

sections.label: Reviewing employee definition, MediSave support
sections.summary: The speaker urges reviewing the employee definition, cites taxi MediSave co-contribution precedent, and seeks training support for freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Whilst we want to retain the flexibility of a gig economy, we should also review the way we define who is an employee in view of today's new employment arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And I am glad that the Minister has earlier mentioned and announced that the Government is seriously considering a support system to the MediSave contribution of freelancers who transact with Government entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There is, Mr Deputy Speaker, already a precedent among taxi operators who co-contribute to taxi drivers' monthly MediSave contributions, that is, the Drive and Save (DAS) scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thirdly and finally, I would like to urge that the Ministry look at enhancing training support for freelancers.

sections.label: Training statistics and funding support
sections.summary: The speaker hopes surveys collect freelancer training and employability statistics and asks about training allowance or absentee payroll support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the Ministry's regular survey, I hope statistics can be collected pertaining to the training status and employability of our freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, can we consider supporting them in their training endeavors with funding help in the form of training allowance or absentee payroll that we offer other workers?

sections.label: Service buyers deduct MediSave contributions
sections.summary: Under the scheme, service buyers deduct a portion of payment to SEPs for the workers' MediSave accounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The scheme will see service buyers deduct a portion of their payment to SEPs to contribute to the workers' MediSave accounts.

sections.label: Prolonged Medical Leave insurance for SEPs
sections.summary: The Ministry worked with NTUC Income and Gigacover to offer SEPs Prolonged Medical Leave insurance paying $60 to $80 a day.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Based on the Tripartite Workgroup's recommendations, the Ministry worked with insurers NTUC Income and Gigacover to offer Prolonged Medical Leave insurance to SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The insurance provides income of $60 to $80 a day for hospitalisation and prolonged medical leave.

sections.label: SEP retirement savings gap and CAYE
sections.summary: A 2018 Manulife survey found SEPs' average savings gap was 55% larger than regular employees; SEPs could opt in to CAYE contributions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A Manulife survey in 2018 found that in reference to a $1 million retirement savings target, the average savings gap of SEPs was 55% larger than regular employees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, SEPs could opt in to contribute 10% of their income up to the monthly contribution ceiling of $6,000 through the CAYE scheme.

sections.label: SEP share of workforce
sections.summary: SEPs make up 8% to 10% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: SEPs make up 8% to 10% of our workforce.

sections.label: Tripartite Standard coverage of SEPs
sections.summary: As of July 2019, 47,000 workers were covered by the Tripartite Standard, adopted by 600 employers, barely a quarter of 200,000 SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a recent reply to a question by the hon Member Assoc Prof Walter Theseira, Minister Josephine Teo said that, as of July 2019, 47,000 workers were covered by the Tripartite Standard for Contracting with SEPs, as adopted by 600 employers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This barely covers a quarter of the 200,000 SEPs reliant on proper contracting to earn their living.

sections.label: Making Tripartite Standard mandatory
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Tripartite Standard should be made mandatory for all companies seeking to contract with SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As fundamental practices, should not the Tripartite Standard be made mandatory for all companies seeking to contract with SEPs?

sections.label: Reviewing SEP classification and protections
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Government should systematically review SEP classification, and lists argued measures including WICA coverage and mandatory Tripartite Standard.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If so, should not the Government conduct a systematic review of all classification of SEPs, especially in key sectors of the gig economy?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have argued that WICA should cover SEPs, that we should legislate for income protection in oligopolistic sectors, that we should encourage regular voluntary CPF contributions using incentives, that there should be SkillsFuture schemes targeted at upskilling SEPs, that the Tripartite Standard for Contracting with Self-Employed Persons be made mandatory, that the test of dependency might be applied to the current classification of SEPs contracted to platform companies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When this Bill is passed, we will be able to help SEPs contribute to CPF through the CAYE mechanism.

sections.label: Legislative basis for SEP contributions
sections.summary: This passage states the legislative basis for regulations requiring SEPs to contribute to MediSave, replaced by new sections 9A and 9B on CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is the legislative basis for regulations requiring SEPs to contribute to MediSave.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will be replaced by the new section 9A, which states that SEPs must contribute to CPF.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To support CAYE, the new section 9B requires collectors who engage and pay SEPs to make contributions to CPF on their behalf.

sections.label: SEP CPF contribution history
sections.summary: This passage states no policy required SEPs to contribute to CPF in those years, and only in 1992 were SEPs first required to contribute, for MediSave only.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As far as I can tell, no policy required SEPs to contribute to CPF during those years, although the text of section 77(1)(e) was amended in 1973 to the present format.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It was only in 1992 that SEPs were first required to contribute to CPF, for MediSave only.

sections.label: Affirming intent for SEP CPF contributions
sections.summary: This passage urges Parliament to affirm that one part of the Bill's intent is to permanently have SEPs contribute to CPF.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, I urge Parliament to affirm that one part of the intent of this Bill is to permanently have SEPs contribute to CPF.

sections.label: SEP earnings and CAYE coverage
sections.summary: This passage states 2017 earnings figures for primary own account workers and says CAYE must eventually give higher-earning SEPs the same CPF coverage employees obtain.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2017, nearly 60% of primary own account workers earned more than $20,000 a year, and 40% earned more than $30,000 a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employees who earn such incomes are able to contribute for their own CPF.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, the CAYE scheme must eventually give such higher-earning SEPs the same coverage that employees obtain from CPF today.

sections.label: CAYE reducing SEP-employee wage gap
sections.summary: This passage states CAYE will reduce the gap between SEPs and employees in take-home wages and help reduce the effect of this wage distortion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CAYE, when implemented, will reduce the gap between SEPs and employees in take-home wages, and will help to reduce the effect of this important distortion in wages.

sections.label: CAYE managing SEP incomes
sections.summary: This passage states CAYE could help SEPs manage incomes by taking greater contributions from high earning periods and lower or no contributions when earnings are low.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CAYE could be used to help SEPs manage their incomes, by taking a greater share of contributions from high earning periods, and lower contributions or even no contributions, when earnings are low.

sections.label: CPF coverage for SEPs
sections.summary: Singapore can lead in sustainably providing social protection for gig economy workers, and Parliament is urged to affirm moving towards full CPF coverage of SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore can take the lead in showing that we can sustainably provide social protection even for gig economy workers and other emerging types of employment in the future economy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge Parliament to affirm that we should move eventually towards full coverage of SEPs through the CPF system.

sections.label: Employers of taxi drivers
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh said some employers such as taxi operators give drivers support and uniforms, so drivers should be classified as employees with statutory protection like CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh earlier mentioned that some employers of, for example, taxi operators, and the likes of it, provide some kind support and maybe even uniform to the drivers, who therefore, they should be classified as employees and given statutory protection, such as CPF contributions and the likes of it.

sections.label: Gig economy dependency criteria
sections.summary: The speaker cites Australia, where gig economy platform features make SEPs look like employees, and says company control and dependency are important criteria for classification.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: I am not alluding to taxi companies because they are not platform companies, so to speak.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: I am talking about the case of Australia where because of the gig economy and the use of online technologies and platform engagement technologies, there are certain features that come of that, in which SEPs start to look like employees because of certain kinds of incentives and membership-tiering, and all these kinds of features, and also the kind of conditions that are being placed on the SEPs to adopt.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: So, the direction and the dependency on the companies' control and direction are important criteria in judging whether these are actually employees and not contract workers.

sections.label: Dependency test for SEPs
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider a dependency test to classify SEPs into employment models, which the speaker says is not very different from what the Member called for.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I am suggesting that the Government consider the use of the test of dependency to look at the classification of SEPs to see whether they fit into certain models of employment and I do not think that is very different from what the Member has actually called for himself.

sections.label: Freelancers treated as employees
sections.summary: The speaker called for certain freelancers, such as food delivery riders, who are asked to come at set hours, take equipment and wear uniforms, to be treated as employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
sentences.text: What I called for is that there are certain groups of freelancers, for example, food delivery riders, who are asked to come at certain hours, take the equipment, wear the uniform, and do the work as though they are employees.

sections.label: CAYE and MediSave payments
sections.summary: SEP MediSave contribution rates stay the same, but CAYE changes the payment process by having service buyers make regular MediSave payments on SEPs' behalf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While SEPs’ MediSave contribution rates remain the same, CAYE changes the payment process itself by having service buyers contribute regular payments to MediSave on SEPs’ behalf.

sections.label: Penalties for payment delays
sections.summary: MOM is asked whether it will consider penalties for undue payment delays to encourage prompt payments by service buyers and GPEs in the pilot phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will MOM consider introducing penalties for undue payment delays, to encourage prompt payments by service buyers, and GPEs in particular, for the pilot phase?

sections.label: SEPs, CAYE and work injury insurance
sections.summary: The passage asks whether SEPs can sign up for CAYE and compel service buyers to opt in, and advocates compulsory work injury insurance by service buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will these SEPs be able to sign up for CAYE and compel their service buyers to opt in to this system for them?

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Beyond CAYE, more can be done to support SEPs holistically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have previously advocated for the compulsory provision of work injury insurance by service buyers to ensure that SEPs have recourse if they suffer injuries in the course of their employment.

sections.label: SEPs procuring their own insurance
sections.summary: The passage states that even if SEPs procure their own insurance coverage, responsible SEPs who buy such insurance need help against undercutting by peers who do not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even if SEPs end up with the responsibility of procuring insurance coverage for themselves, we need to help responsible SEPs who purchase such insurance guard against undercutting by peers who do not.

sections.label: CPF amendments for SEPs
sections.summary: The passage supports CPF amendments, notes about 200,000 SEPs and that one in four cannot keep up with annual MediSave contributions, and welcomes help for about 6,000 SEPs through CAYE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay)  : I support the proposed amendments to this Bill, which will ensure that the CPF system remains relevant to the changes in the job landscape and employment practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There are many challenges faced by freelancers or SEPs who are estimated to number around 200,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In fact, one out of four SEPs is unable to keep up with their obligations to contribute to their MediSave account annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I welcome the amendments that will help about 6,000 SEPs who provide services to the Government to make automatic MediSave contributions through a CAYE scheme.

sections.label: CPF Pilot for CAYE
sections.summary: The Minister announced that the CPF Pilot for CAYE will start in January 2020 with SEPs providing services directly to the Government or the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Minister announced that the CPF Pilot for CAYE will start in January 2020 with SEPs providing services directly to the Government or the public sector.

sections.label: SEPs and MediSave obligations
sections.summary: The passage states that one in four SEPs has not kept up with their MediSave obligations annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As previously reported, one in four SEPs has not kept up with their MediSave obligations annually.

sections.label: CAYE and SEP MediSave
sections.summary: Members acknowledged the CAYE pilot will help SEPs meet MediSave obligations through smaller, more regular contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Members of the House have acknowledged that the CAYE pilot will help SEPs meet their MediSave obligations more easily through smaller and more regular contributions.

sections.label: Tripartite Standard on Contracting
sections.summary: The Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs was launched to reduce payment-related disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As such, we have launched the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs to reduce payment-related disputes.

sections.label: Prolonged medical leave insurance
sections.summary: PML products were introduced with insurers, and close to 30,000 SEPs are now covered by PML insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To protect SEPs from the loss of income due to prolonged illness or injury, we have worked with insurers to introduce prolonged medical leave (PML) products.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I am pleased to update both Mr Arasu Duraisamy and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh that close to 30,000 SEPs are now covered by PML insurance.

sections.label: Piloting CAYE
sections.summary: CAYE is being piloted to complete follow-up to the Tripartite Workgroup's recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To complete the follow-up to the Tripartite Workgroup's recommendations, we are now piloting CAYE.

sections.label: No private sector extension
sections.summary: There are currently no plans to extend CAYE to the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Currently, there are no plans to extend CAYE to the private sector.

sections.label: SEP cash flow and opt out
sections.summary: SEPs keeping up with contributions may opt out, while CAYE will help about 600 affected SEPs avoid snowballing arrears.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Zainal Sapari also raised an important concern that SEPs may face cash flow constraints as they transition to this new scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will allow SEPs to opt out if they have been keeping up with their contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For the small group of about 600 affected SEPs who are not keeping up, CAYE will certainly help them to avoid snowballing arrears.

sections.label: Transport company work pass suspension
sections.summary: A transport and logistics company was given a stern warning and had its work pass privileges suspended for misclassifying its driver as an SEP.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In one case which we handled recently, a transport and logistics company was issued with a stern warning and had its work pass privileges suspended for misclassifying its driver as an SEP.

sections.label: CAYE and SEP CPF obligations
sections.summary: There is no change to the CPF obligations of SEPs under CAYE.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To summarise again on CAYE, there is no change to the CPF obligations of SEPs.

sections.label: New rules for RSS and CPF LIFE
sections.summary: Under the new rules, members receiving RSS payouts get the same or higher payouts, while CPF LIFE members are unaffected and continue monthly payouts for life.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With the new rules, members already receiving RSS payouts will either get the same or higher payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Members who are on CPF LIFE will not be affected at all and will continue receiving monthly payouts for life.

sections.label: Roadshow visitor numbers
sections.summary: The roadshows are held over five weekends across the island and received about 170,000 visitors this year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These roadshows are held over five weekends across the island.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This year alone, the roadshows received about 170,000 visitors.

sections.label: Centre customer numbers in 2018
sections.summary: In 2018 alone, these centres received one million customers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2018 alone, these centres received one million customers.

sections.label: Initiative numbers since 2016
sections.summary: Since the initiative started in 2016, more than 36,000 have been served.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since this initiative started in 2016, more than 36,000 have been served.

sections.label: Call centre phone calls
sections.summary: In 2018, the call centre received about 660,000 phone calls.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2018, the call centre received about 660,000 phone calls.

sections.label: CPF Board app and outreach
sections.summary: Over 97% said they would recommend it, and CPF Board redesigned its mobile app and plans posters and Silver Generation Office engagement.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over 97% said that they would recommend it to others.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: CPF Board has also recently redesigned its mobile app, giving members easy access to their CPF details and transactions like making top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, CPF Board will be putting out a series of educational posters in housing estates to clarify common CPF misconceptions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are working with the Silver Generation Office to engage older members.

sections.label: Voluntary PML insurance for SEPs
sections.summary: The approach is to keep PML insurance voluntary for SEPs, as taxi companies may pass costs to drivers and SEPs should decide their own protection.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is potentially the company that leases out the taxis.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But he is also very right to say from the taxi companies' point of view then, it is entirely possible that they choose to recover these costs through higher rental costs which would impact the drivers without necessarily giving them an opportunity to recover this cost from the commuters which is why, I think, our thinking is not to be hasty about making PML insurance compulsory.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think the fact that the individuals choose to be SEPs, we have to give them the ability to decide for themselves what kinds of protection are relevant to them.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If they were comfortable with the present arrangements and do not see much need for this kind of protection to be made compulsory, it may not be right for us to insist on it for now.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It does not mean that all of them do not wish to move into regular employment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, our approach right now is to keep it voluntary and then, with a good base load of insured persons – in fact, the insurance premiums could be brought down, and if the insurance premiums have been brought down, then to the SEPs, they will do their sums and see whether it is useful to them, considering the benefits that come with it.
